```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  fig.path = "../man/figures/",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4
)

scc_available <- nchar(Sys.which("scc")) > 0L
rlang_path    <- glockr:::fetch_rlang_source()
if (is.na(rlang_path)) {
  message("rlang source unavailable; downstream chunks shown but not evaluated.")
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
  rlang_path <- ""
}
```

```{r library}
library(glockr)
```

## Generated and minified files

`scc` can detect files that were auto-generated or minified. Detection is
**opt-in**: pass `gen = TRUE` to identify generated files and `min = TRUE` to
identify minified files. Use `min_gen = TRUE` (`-z`) to enable both at once.

```{r gen-min, eval = FALSE}
# identify generated files; generated column reflects detection
scc_by_file(rlang_path, gen = TRUE)[, c("filename", "generated", "minified")]
#> # A tibble: 383 × 3
#>    filename     generated minified
#>    <chr>        <lgl>     <lgl>
#>  1 sink.R       FALSE     FALSE
#>  2 testthat.R   FALSE     FALSE
#>  3 c-lib.R      FALSE     FALSE
#>  4 aaa-topics.R FALSE     FALSE
#>  5 test-obj.R   FALSE     FALSE
#>  6 quo.R        FALSE     FALSE
#>  7 nse-inject.R FALSE     FALSE
#>  8 formula.R    FALSE     FALSE
#>  9 attr.R       FALSE     FALSE
#> 10 helper-cli.R FALSE     FALSE
#> # ℹ 373 more rows
```

### Excluding generated or minified files

`no_gen = TRUE` (implies `gen = TRUE`) detects generated files and drops them
from the results. `no_min = TRUE` does the same for minified files.
`no_min_gen = TRUE` removes both in one pass.

```{r no-gen, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, no_gen     = TRUE)   # drop generated files
scc(rlang_path, no_min     = TRUE)   # drop minified files
scc(rlang_path, no_min_gen = TRUE)   # drop both
```

### Custom generation markers

By default `scc` looks for `"do not edit"` and `"<auto-generated />"` in the
first lines of a file. Override with `generated_markers`:

```{r gen-markers, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path,
    no_gen = TRUE,
    generated_markers = c("GENERATED", "AUTO_BUILT"))
```

### Minified-line threshold

A file is considered minified when its average bytes per line exceeds a
threshold (default 255). Lower it to catch less-aggressively minified files:

```{r min-threshold, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, no_min = TRUE, min_gen_line_length = 100L)
```

## Duplicate detection

`no_duplicates = TRUE` removes files whose content is identical to another
file already counted, keeping only one copy in the totals.

```{r no-dup, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, no_duplicates = TRUE)
```

## Excluding files and directories

### By directory name

`exclude_dir` takes a character vector of directory *names* (not full paths)
to skip entirely. The scc defaults (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`) are always applied;
this extends them.

```{r excl-dir, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, exclude_dir = c("tests", "src"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 10
#>   language files lines  code comments blanks
#>   <chr>    <int> <int> <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1 R           77 25866 12663    10861   2342
#> 2 Markdown    12  8425  6006        0   2419
#> 3 YAML         9   735   587       35    113
#> 4 SVG         10    10    10        0      0
#> 5 License      1     2     2        0      0
#> 6 TOML         1     2     2        0      0
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: complexity <int>,
#> #   weighted_complexity <dbl>, bytes <int>,
#> #   uloc <int>
```

### By file name

`exclude_file` skips files whose *name* (not full path) matches any element:

```{r excl-file, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, exclude_file = c("LICENSE", "testthat.R"))
```

### By path pattern

`not_match` accepts a character vector of regex patterns. Any file whose full
path matches is excluded. Each element becomes a separate `--not-match` flag.

```{r not-match, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, not_match = c("test_", "_generated"))
```

### Symlinks

By default `scc` skips symbolic links. Set `include_symlinks = TRUE` to count
them (no effect on Windows).

```{r symlinks, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, include_symlinks = TRUE)
```

### Ignore files

`scc` respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, `.gitmodules`, and `.sccignore` by
default. Use the corresponding `no_*` flags to disable each:

```{r no-ignore, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, no_gitignore  = TRUE)  # ignore .gitignore rules
scc(rlang_path, no_ignore     = TRUE)  # ignore .ignore rules
scc(rlang_path, no_gitmodule  = TRUE)  # ignore .gitmodules
scc(rlang_path, no_scc_ignore = TRUE)  # ignore .sccignore
```

`count_ignore = TRUE` also *counts* the ignore files themselves as source:

```{r count-ignore, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, count_ignore = TRUE)
```

## Large-file thresholds

`no_large = TRUE` drops files that exceed a byte or line-count threshold.
The defaults are 1 000 000 bytes and 40 000 lines; override with
`large_byte_count` and `large_line_count`.

```{r no-large, eval = FALSE}
# skip files larger than 50 000 bytes or 1 000 lines
scc(rlang_path, no_large = TRUE, large_byte_count = 50000L, large_line_count = 1000L)
```

## Analysing multiple paths

Both `scc()` and `scc_by_file()` accept a character vector of paths, so you
can compare directories side by side:

```{r multi-path, eval = FALSE}
scc(c(
  file.path(rlang_path, "R"),
  file.path(rlang_path, "tests")
))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 10
#>   language files lines  code comments blanks
#>   <chr>    <int> <int> <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1 R          162 44299 27988    10971   5340
#> 2 Markdown    41  8510  7860        0    650
#> 3 C            2    41    33        0      8
#> 4 Makefile     1    11     7        0      4
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: complexity <int>,
#> #   weighted_complexity <dbl>, bytes <int>,
#> #   uloc <int>
```

## Output display flags

These flags affect `scc`'s console/tabular output but do **not** change the
tibble returned by `scc()` or `scc_by_file()`.

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `percent = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Add percentage columns to tabular output |
| `size_unit` | `NULL` (`"si"`) | Size display unit: `"si"`, `"binary"`, `"mixed"`, or `"xkcd-*"` |
| `no_hborder = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Remove horizontal borders from table |
| `no_size = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Hide the size-calculation summary line |
| `character = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Show max/mean characters-per-line columns |
| `verbose = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Verbose processing log (written to stderr) |
| `debug = TRUE` | `FALSE` | Full debug log (written to stdout; may disrupt JSON in some environments) |

```{r display-flags, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path, percent = TRUE, size_unit = "binary")
```

## Performance tuning

On very large repositories you can control the number of worker goroutines and
queue sizes used by `scc`. The defaults work well in most cases; adjust only
when profiling shows a bottleneck.

| Parameter | scc default | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `directory_walker_job_workers` | `8` | Workers scanning directories |
| `file_process_job_workers` | `12` | Workers collecting file stats |
| `file_gc_count` | `10000` | Files parsed before GC runs |
| `file_list_queue_size` | `12` | Queue for discovered files |
| `file_summary_job_queue_size` | `12` | Queue for processed-file stats |

```{r perf, eval = FALSE}
scc(rlang_path,
    directory_walker_job_workers = 4L,
    file_process_job_workers     = 4L,
    file_gc_count                = 5000L)
```

## Supported languages

`scc_languages()` returns every language `scc` recognizes, along with the file
extensions it maps to that language.

```{r languages, eval = FALSE}
langs <- scc_languages()
nrow(langs)
#> [1] 358

head(langs, 10)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 2
#>    language     extensions
#>    <chr>        <chr>
#>  1 ABAP         abap
#>  2 ABNF         abnf
#>  3 ActionScript as
#>  4 Ada          ada,adb,ads,pad
#>  5 Agda         agda
#>  6 Alchemist    crn
#>  7 Alex         x
#>  8 Algol 68     a68
#>  9 Alloy        als
#> 10 Amber        ab
```

Search for a specific language:

```{r lang-search, eval = FALSE}
langs[grepl("^R$", langs$language), ]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   language extensions
#>   <chr>    <chr>
#> 1 R        r
```
